parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the 2025 executive order and Nov 2025 Supreme Court ruling force sex-assigned-at-birth markers; the Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report blocked passports and multiple governments issued advisories — a universal document exposure. A federal bar on trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities plus bans in 21 state/provinces (division: K-12 students only) restrict everyday access. Custody is documented severe: corrections conversion-therapy policy (hair, hormones removed) and immigration detainees reporting beatings and sexual abuse, alongside official 'radically pro-transgender' threat framing. Offsets: no identity criminalisation, no documented violence campaign, federal hate-crime and employment protections, active litigation with several orders enjoined.

entry_documents.exposure: X-marker processing stopped Feb 2025; M/F only per supporting documents; Feb 2025 cable orders refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and possible lifetime fraud finding; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad; at least eight foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on documentation strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or document doubt can escalate into immigration custody, where documented abuse of trans detainees occurs.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 national corrections bureau mandates conversion-therapy policy: short hair, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs; trans prisoner counts unpublished since 2025. Immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no documented custody-specific remedy for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document/entry dispute at the border can lead directly into the custody system where these practices operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; bans in 9+1 units (all government buildings incl. colleges), 9 more (schools and some buildings), 3 (schools only); 4 units criminalise in certain circumstances. Division's 2023 statute restricts public-school students; no statewide adult rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces, 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban; division visitors face no documented adult facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visiting minor entering public schools in the division hits the 2023 statute administered by local districts.

care_services.exposure: Division bars gender-affirming care for minors (effective 14 July 2023, no phase-out, upheld through appeal Sept 2023); national orders and proposed insurance rules target minors' care and describe it as mutilation.
care_services.protection: Adult emergency care not documented as restricted; several national orders enjoined or litigated.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor could be refused continuation of prescribed care by division providers; application to non-resident visitors is not stated.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Justice department reward guidance and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy single out groups 'radically pro-transgender'; executive orders direct investigation of 'gender ideology' and describe minors' care as mutilation; 66% of residents back sex-at-birth document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; 'gender ideology' is not a reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the severity of any police or administrative encounter once a visitor is identified.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division: birth-sex school facilities, care ban with no phase-out, 2022 school sports ban. National: order threatening prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, sports and care orders for minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy on minors banned division-wide since Sept 2024; national employment protection applies.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces care refusal, school-facility rules and heightened scrutiny if identity surfaces.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute covers sexual orientation but expressly excludes gender identity; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes; 2013 religious-freedom statute gives a route around local ordinances; no trans-specific violence data for the division.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a 2011 bias beating produced arrests and guilty pleas; no sodomy law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak state-level enhancement leaves an attacked visitor dependent on federal charges and uneven local policing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Rules shift with litigation: Nov 2025 Supreme Court let passport restrictions take effect; enforcement frequency of the school facility provision, service-refusal application of the religious statute, and later status of the care ban are unquantified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ; 19 municipalities with gender-identity non-discrimination ordinances; federal employment and hate-crime protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor's exposure depends on which measures are operative at the moment and place of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: like Veluna, an unremedied birth-sex facility restriction operates in government settings with no offence of being trans and polite private encounters. This dossier adds an entry-document regime with refusal and lifetime-fraud exposure plus documented custody abuse, so it sits slightly lower despite functioning litigation.

Lower than Veleda. Veleda's worst feature is unremedied invasive searches at transport with acknowledged-but-persistent violations. Here the border document rule can refuse entry or impose lifetime ineligibility, and corrections/immigration custody practices are more severe than screening searches.

Higher than Savorek. Savorek adds recurrent police stops with extortion threats, a facility rule covering all public facilities and hospitals, and rejected complaints — routes not documented here. But this dossier's custody conversion-therapy and immigration-abuse record is comparably severe, so the gap is modest.

Materially below Valess. Valess combines a tolerated gender-diverse tradition, accepted foreign documents, a dead-letter statute and one compensated refusal. Here documents, facilities and custody all carry documented state-imposed exposure; no traditional acceptance or working visitor remedy is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Federal and division rules combine into one restrictive system for the traveller. The document regime is the sharpest universal exposure: markers fixed to assigned sex, visa adjudication instructed to refuse doubtful cases, possible lifetime fraud finding, corroborated by foreign travel advisories and stranded travellers. Facility exclusion follows at federal sites and in 21 units (the division limits its rule to school students). If discovery leads to detention, the record shows hormone withdrawal, forced haircuts and abuse in immigration custody — with official rhetoric framing pro-trans advocacy as extremist. Remedy exists but is partial and reactive: courts have enjoined several orders yet allowed the passport rule to stand; federal hate-crime and employment protections coexist with a division hate-crime statute that omits gender identity and a religious-exemption route around local ordinances. No criminalisation of identity, no organised street targeting, and no trans-specific violence data — so severity, not street violence, drives the score.
